mainTopic: Partners guarding for each other, and when a person who has a stake in a field may not testify about it (the case of ראובן, שמעון, לוי, and יהודה)
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: why partners who guard for each other are not exempt under the rule of שמירה בבעלים. רב פפא answers that they take turns, each guarding on a different day. Then the גמרא brings a ברייתא: someone who sold a house or field cannot testify for the buyer, but someone who sold a cow or cloak can. The גמרא asks why there is a difference. רב ששת explains the first clause through a stolen-field case: ראובן stole a field from שמעון and sold it to לוי, and then יהודה claimed it. שמעון may not testify for לוי, because he wants the field to stay with לוי so he can later take it back. The גמרא asks how שמעון could take it back after testifying, and answers that he only said the field is not יהודה's. It then asks why שמעון would care who holds the field, since his right is the same against both. Two answers follow: לוי is an easier opponent, or both שמעון and יהודה have witnesses, so the land would stay with יהודה for good while שמעון can still win it back from לוי.

steps.title: Why aren't the partners exempt as guarding with the owner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges an earlier ruling that partners who guard each other's property are liable like paid guardians. Each partner is working for the other, so this should count as שמירה בבעלים, which brings an exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are they liable? This is guarding while the owner is also working for the guardian!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the ruling it just quoted, that partners who guard for each other are treated as paid guardians.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that when the owner is working for the guardian at the time the guarding begins, the guardian is exempt. That rule is called שמירה בבעלים. Here both partners guard for each other at once, so each one is the 'owner' working for the other. That should give them the exemption, not make them liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarding where the owner is also working for the guardian. This frees the guardian from paying.

steps.confusionAlert: This line continues a discussion that started before this section, about partners guarding each other's things. It is not part of the ברייתא about selling that comes next.

phrases.english: Why?
phrases.notes: Why should the partners be liable as paid guardians, as was just ruled?

phrases.english: It is guarding with the owner!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling from before this section that partners guarding for each other are liable as paid guardians.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that guarding partners are liable like paid guardians.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each partner works for the other at the same time, so the exemption of שמירה בבעלים should apply.

steps.title: Each partner guards on a different day
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the case is where one partner said: guard for me today and I will guard for you tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is where he told him, 'Guard for me today, and I will guard for you tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. The partners are not guarding at the same moment; they take turns on different days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמירה בבעלים only works if the owner is working for the guardian at the same time. When they take turns, on any given day only one person is guarding. The owner is not working for him that day, so there is no exemption. The payment for each day's guarding is the other day's guarding, so each counts as a paid guardian.
steps.whatToRemember: Partners who guard for each other in turns are liable as paid guardians. The exemption of שמירה בבעלים does not apply because they never guard at the same time.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is where he said to him:
Guard for me today,
and I will guard for you tomorrow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to guarding on different days.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The partners guard for each other at the same time, so the exemption should apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: They take turns, so the owner is never working for the guardian at the time of guarding.

steps.title: A seller testifying for his buyer: land versus movable items
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: someone who sold a house or field cannot testify for the buyer, because he carries responsibility for it. Someone who sold a cow or cloak can testify, because he does not carry responsibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If he sold him a house or a field, he cannot testify for him about it, because the responsibility for it is on him. If he sold him a cow or a cloak, he can testify for him about it, because the responsibility for it is not on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about when a seller may testify for the buyer about the item he sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone challenges the buyer's ownership, the seller would normally have to pay the buyer back. That money is his אחריות. A seller who would have to pay has a personal interest, so his testimony is not accepted. The ברייתא says this applies to land but not to a cow or a cloak. Why, it does not say.

keyTerms.meaning: Responsibility to pay the buyer back if the item is taken from him

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר לוֹ בַּיִת, מָכַר לוֹ שָׂדֶה –
phrases.english: If he sold him a house, or sold him a field,
he may not testify for him about it,
because the responsibility for it is on him.

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר לוֹ פָּרָה, מָכַר לוֹ טַלִּית –
phrases.english: If he sold him a cow, or sold him a cloak,
he may testify for him about it,
because the responsibility for it is not on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָכַר לוֹ בַּיִת, מָכַר לוֹ שָׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic unrelated to the guarding discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller of land may not testify for the buyer, because he is responsible for it. A seller of movable items may testify, because he is not.

steps.title: Why the difference between the two clauses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the first clause (house or field) different from the second (cow or cloak).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first part, and what is different about the last part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's split between land and movable items. This sets up רב ששת's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every seller is normally responsible if the item turns out to be stolen, whether it is land or a cow. So it is not clear why the ברייתא says the land seller has responsibility and the cow seller does not. The גמרא wants a case that explains the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: What is different about the first part,
and what is different about the last part?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a seller of land counts as having responsibility, and a seller of movable items does not.

steps.title: רב ששת: the stolen field case
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains the first clause through a story. ראובן stole a field from שמעון and sold it to לוי, and then יהודה claims it. שמעון may not testify for לוי, because he wants the field to go back to לוי so he can later take it from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The first part is about ראובן, who stole a field from שמעון and sold it to לוי, and then יהודה came and challenged it. שמעון may not go testify for לוי, because he is pleased that it should go back to לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a specific case to explain why the first clause disqualifies the witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land cannot really be stolen; it stays in its true owner's name. So שמעון can always take his field back from whoever holds it. If the field stays with לוי, שמעון can later take it from him. That gives שמעון a personal reason to want לוי to win against יהודה, and someone with a personal reason cannot testify.

keyTerms.meaning: It suits him; he is pleased with it

steps.confusionAlert: In רב ששת's case, the person who may not testify is שמעון, the victim of the theft. It is not ראובן, the one who actually sold the field.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
The first part is about Reuven, who stole a field from Shimon,
and sold it to Levi,
and Yehuda came and is challenging it;
that Shimon may not go
to testify for Levi,
because he is pleased that it should go back.
phrases.notes: He wants the field to return to Levi, so that he can later take it from Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: רֵישָׁא – בִּרְאוּבֵן שֶׁגָּזַל שָׂדֶה מִשִּׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the first clause disqualifies the witness.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first clause is about a stolen field. The victim, שמעון, wants it to stay with לוי so that he can later take it back, so he is biased.

steps.title: After testifying for לוי, how can שמעון take it back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if שמעון testified that the field belongs to לוי, how could he later take it away from לוי?
steps.simpleTranslation: But once he testified that it is לוי's, how can he take it away from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's case. Testifying for לוי would seem to block שמעון from ever claiming the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמעון says in court 'this field belongs to לוי,' he cannot later turn around and say it is his own. That would contradict his own words. If so, he gains nothing by helping לוי, and there is no reason to suspect him of bias.

phrases.english: But since he testified for him that it is Levi's,
how can he take it away from him?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that שמעון gains by having the field go to לוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own testimony that the field is לוי's would stop him from later claiming it, so he has nothing to gain.

steps.title: He only testified that it is not יהודה's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמעון's testimony was only 'I know this land is not יהודה's.' He never said it belongs to לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he says: 'I know that this land is not יהודה's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing what שמעון actually said in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון only denied יהודה's claim. He never said the field belongs to לוי. So nothing he said stops him from later saying it is really his own, and he can still take it from לוי.

phrases.english: It is where he says: I know
that this land is not Yehuda's.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר: יָדַעְנָא דְּהַאי אַרְעָא דְּלָאו דִּיהוּדָה הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the wording of the testimony.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמעון testified that the field is לוי's, which would stop him from claiming it later.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only testified that it is not יהודה's, so he can still claim it from לוי later.

steps.title: He could take it from יהודה just as easily
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. Whatever right lets שמעון take the field from לוי would also let him take it from יהודה, so he gains nothing by helping לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with that same right that lets him take it from לוי, let him take it from יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge against רב ששת's case. The next step answers it, and step 10 gives a second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון's claim comes from being the true owner whose field was stolen. That claim works the same against anyone holding the field, לוי or יהודה. So it should not matter to him who wins the case, and his testimony should not be seen as biased.

phrases.english: But with that same right
by which he takes it from Levi,
let him take it from Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְהָהוּא זְכוּתָא דְּקָא מַפֵּיק לַהּ מִלֵּוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 7 settles the first problem, this raises a new challenge against רב ששת's case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמעון is biased toward having the field stay with לוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His ownership claim works equally against לוי and יהודה, so he has no reason to prefer לוי and is not biased.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge goes to the heart of רב ששת's explanation. Steps 9 and 10 each show a different reason why שמעון still has something to gain.

steps.title: שמעון prefers to fight with לוי rather than יהודה
steps.stepSummary: שמעון gains by testifying because לוי is an easier opponent in court than יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because שמעון says: the second one (לוי) is easy for me to deal with, but the first one (יהודה) is harder than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 8. Even if שמעון has the same legal right against both people, he would rather face לוי in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said שמעון gains nothing, because his right against לוי is the same as his right against יהודה. This answer says the gain is practical, not legal: לוי is easier to deal with. That personal advantage is enough to make שמעון's testimony biased.

keyTerms.meaning: Easy for me, someone I can deal with comfortably
Harder than him, a tougher opponent

phrases.english: Because he says: the second one is easy for me,
phrases.notes: "He" is שמעון. "The second one" is לוי, the man who bought the field.

phrases.english: the first one is harder than him.
phrases.notes: "The first one" is יהודה, the man now claiming the field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by showing a practical gain for שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical motive: the bias comes from preferring one opponent over another, not from a legal difference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since שמעון's legal right is the same against לוי and against יהודה, he gains nothing and should be allowed to testify.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמעון still gains because לוי is easier to fight in court, so he is a biased witness.

steps.title: When both sides have witnesses, the land stays where it is
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: if both שמעון and יהודה have witnesses, the land stays with whoever holds it, so שמעון could only win it back from לוי, never from יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: this is a case where this person (שמעון) has witnesses and that person (יהודה) has witnesses, and the רבנן said that in such a case the land stays where it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the challenge from step 8. It describes a case where שמעון's right against לוי is actually stronger than his right against יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמעון and יהודה both bring witnesses, the witnesses cancel out and the land stays with whoever holds it. If יהודה won the field, שמעון could never take it from him. But לוי only has the field because he bought it from the thief ראובן, so שמעון can take it back from לוי. That is a real legal gain, so שמעון is biased.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces a second, different answer
Where it stands, let it stay: the land remains with whoever holds it

steps.whatToRemember: שמעון cannot testify for לוי because he gains from לוי winning. One answer says לוי is an easier opponent. The other says that if יהודה wins and both sides have witnesses, the land stays with יהודה forever, but שמעון can still take it from לוי.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמעון's witnesses help him against יהודה. Because יהודה also has witnesses, the two sets cancel out, and that is exactly why שמעון would lose for good if יהודה got the land.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a witness counts as biased even when his gain is hidden. Here the gain is keeping open his own path to get the field back later.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
such as where this master has witnesses
phrases.notes: "This master" is שמעון, and "that master" in the next line is יהודה.

phrases.english: and that master has witnesses,
and the Sages said:
the land, where it stands, let it stay.
phrases.notes: He means the land stays with whoever is holding it right now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the קשיא of step 8, alongside step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing: sets up a case where שמעון's legal power against לוי is stronger than against יהודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמעון's right to the field is equal against anyone who holds it, so helping לוי gains him nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: When both שמעון and יהודה have witnesses, the land stays with the holder. If יהודה held it, שמעון would lose for good. With לוי holding it, שמעון can reclaim it, so he is biased.
